faq.q: What does “the beat goes on” mean?
faq.a: It means life keeps moving forward no matter what happens. It is both an acceptance that time doesn’t stop and an encouragement that you can keep going too.

faq.q: Where does the phrase “the beat goes on” come from?
faq.a: It is best known from the 1967 Sonny & Cher song “The Beat Goes On,” written by Sonny Bono.

faq.q: Is “the beat goes on” a positive or negative phrase?
faq.a: It can be either. It can feel hard when you are grieving and the world keeps moving, but it is also hopeful because no moment, good or bad, lasts forever.

faq.q: How do I find my own rhythm in life?
faq.a: Notice when you feel rushed or stuck, stop comparing your pace to others, and build small daily rituals that steady you.

faq.q: How can I keep going when life feels like it stopped?
faq.a: Slow down, focus only on the next small step, and let people who care about you help. If it feels too heavy for too long, reach out to a counselor or doctor.

faq.q: When do people say “the beat goes on”?
faq.a: People often say it after big changes like a retirement, graduation, loss, or breakup, or simply to note that life continues.
